attributes.description: Bench numbers for VALUES zip, TOP zip, and Kibana search_after span derivation from .rule-events.
attributes.panelsJSON:
[{"type":"markdown","embeddableConfig":{"title":"Pattern A / B and query methods","content":"Line charts plot **successful runs only**. A series that stops is a 429 (or missing size), not a speedup.

**Filter:** use the `test_id` control (this dashboard is set to `2026-08-29-a10k`). The original ingest is `2026-08-29`.

## What these series mean

Two axes: **data shape** (A vs B) and **algorithm** (VALUES zip / TOP zip / search_after).

### Pattern A vs Pattern B

Synthetic `.rule-events` for one `episode.id`, 1-minute rule interval.

| | Pattern A | Pattern B |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Flap style | all-flip | longer runs |
| `run_len` | 1 | typically 10 |
| Relationship | flaps = docs | flaps ≈ docs / 10 |
| Example | 1000 docs → 1000 spans | 1000 docs → ~100 spans |
| Stresses | every row is a status change | same window, fewer spans |

Same `docs` = same 1m-rule window. A is worst-case flapping; B is closer to real episodes with stable runs.

### VALUES zip vs TOP zip vs search_after

How spans are derived (not different data).

| Method | Where | Returns | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **VALUES zip** | ES\|QL in ES | full span geometry: start, end, `duration_ms`, `data` | pack rows into `VALUES()`, `MV_ZIP` twice, expand. Last ES-direct success: A **1000** flaps, B **2000** docs / 200 flaps |
| **TOP zip** | ES\|QL in ES | **span starts only** (no duration / end) | `TOP(@timestamp, 10000, "asc", …)`, one expand. Cheaper; last ES-direct success: A **2000**, B **4000** / 400 |
| **TOP zip + Kibana duration** (`top_zip_kibana_duration`) | Kibana HTTP probe | TOP zip starts, then Kibana attaches `duration_ms` / `status_ended_at` | Kibana reduce <10 ms; still dies at 10k on ES (`esql_block_factory`). Last HTTP success: **5k / 500** |
| **search_after** | Query DSL PIT + Kibana RLE | full spans | page events (2000), run-length-encode in Kibana. Cheap through **10k events / 1k flaps** (~102 ms) |
| **ES\|QL + Kibana RLE** (`esql`) | one-shot ES\|QL `KEEP`/`SORT`/`LIMIT 10000` + Kibana RLE | full spans | one ES\|QL round-trip, same reducer as search_after. Assumes episode < 10k events |

Series like `A / top_zip` = Pattern A data + TOP zip query. `A / values_zip` = same A data, VALUES zip query.

**Why A looks slower on TOP zip:** same `docs`, more span rows (every event is a transition). search_after tracks **docs**, not flaps, so A vs B at the same window is about the same.
